title: Why Did No One Say the Emperor Was Naked?
subtitle: 為什麼沒人說國王沒穿衣服？安徒生〈國王的新衣〉
source: 原創導讀；故事原文依 Project Gutenberg《Andersen's Fairy Tales》（公版英譯），背景依 Wikipedia〈The Emperor's New Clothes〉，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Hans Christian Andersen, Andersen's Fairy Tales, Project Gutenberg

beginner.title: The Invisible Clothes
paras: Once there was an emperor who loved new clothes more than anything. He spent all his money on them. One day, two tricksters came to town. They said they could make magic cloth. Anyone who was stupid, or not good at their job, would not be able to see it. He had a different suit for every hour of the day.
從前有一位國王，他愛新衣服勝過一切，把所有的錢都花在衣服上。有一天，兩個騙子來到城裡。他們說自己會織一種神奇的布，任何笨蛋或不適任的人，都看不見它。他一天中的每個小時都換一套不同的衣服。

The emperor paid them a lot of money. The tricksters pretended to weave, but there was nothing on their machines. The emperor’s officials came to look. They saw nothing, but they did not want to seem stupid, so they all said, “How beautiful!” Even the emperor said the same.
國王付了他們很多錢。騙子假裝在織布，但織布機上什麼都沒有。國王的官員們來看，他們什麼也沒看到，但不想顯得自己很笨，所以都說：「好美啊！」連國王也這麼說。

Finally, the emperor “wore” his new clothes in a big parade through the city. All the people said, “What wonderful clothes!” No one wanted to look foolish. Then a little child shouted, “But the Emperor has nothing at all on!” Soon everyone was saying it. The child’s father said, “Listen to the voice of innocence!”
最後，國王「穿著」他的新衣服，在城裡舉行盛大的遊行。所有人都說：「多麼美麗的衣服啊！」沒有人想顯得愚蠢。這時，一個小孩大喊：「可是國王什麼都沒穿啊！」很快地，每個人都這麼說了。孩子的父親說：「聽聽這天真無邪的聲音！」

The emperor knew they were right. But he kept walking proudly, and his servants kept holding up a train that was not there. The Danish writer Hans Christian Andersen published this story in 1837, and it has been translated into more than 100 languages.
國王知道大家說得對。但他還是驕傲地繼續往前走，他的侍從們也繼續托著根本不存在的衣襬。丹麥作家漢斯．克里斯汀．安徒生在 1837 年發表了這個故事，它已被翻譯成一百多種語言。

Why did no one speak? Each person thought everyone else could see the clothes. Psychologists call this “pluralistic ignorance”. Today, people say “the emperor has no clothes” when everyone pretends something is true. It takes courage to be the child who says what everyone sees.
為什麼沒有人說話？每個人都以為其他人看得到那件衣服。心理學家把這叫作「多數無知」。今天，當大家都假裝某件事是真的時，人們會說「國王沒穿衣服」。要當那個說出大家都看到的事實的孩子，需要勇氣。

intermediate.title: Why Did No One Say the Emperor Was Naked?
paras: Hans Christian Andersen’s “The Emperor’s New Clothes” begins with a ruler so fond of new clothes that he spends all his money on them and cares little for his soldiers or his duties. Two rogues arrive claiming to be weavers. Their cloth, they say, has a wonderful property: it is invisible to anyone who is “unfit for the office he held” or unusually foolish. He has a different suit for every hour of the day, and instead of saying the emperor is “in council”, people say he is “sitting in his wardrobe”.
安徒生的〈國王的新衣〉一開頭，就是一位極度喜愛新衣服的統治者，他把所有的錢都花在衣服上，卻不太關心他的士兵和職責。兩個自稱織工的騙子來了。他們說，自己織的布有一種神奇的特性：凡是「不適任其職位」或特別愚蠢的人，都看不見它。他一天中每個小時都換一套衣服；人們不說國王「在議事」，而是說他「坐在衣櫥裡」。

The trick works because of fear. The emperor sends his most trusted ministers to inspect the work. Each sees empty looms but praises the cloth rather than admit he cannot see it, because admitting it would suggest he is unfit for his job. Eventually the emperor himself looks, sees nothing, and also pretends.
這個騙局之所以成功，是因為恐懼。國王派他最信任的大臣去檢查。每個人都看到空空的織布機，卻都稱讚這塊布，而不願承認自己看不見，因為承認就等於暗示自己不適任。最後，國王親自去看，什麼也沒看到，也跟著假裝。

The story reaches its climax during a grand procession. Crowds along the streets admire the invisible clothes until a little child cries out, “But the Emperor has nothing at all on!” The words spread, and soon the whole crowd repeats them. The emperor realises they are right, yet he decides the procession must go on, and his servants keep holding up a train that does not exist.
故事的高潮發生在一場盛大的遊行中。街道兩旁的群眾都在讚美那件看不見的衣服，直到一個小孩喊出：「可是國王什麼都沒穿啊！」這句話傳開了，很快整群人都跟著喊。國王明白大家說得對，卻決定遊行必須繼續，他的侍從們也繼續托著一條根本不存在的衣襬。

Andersen published the tale in 1837, alongside “The Little Mermaid”. He based it on a medieval Spanish story from 1335, which he knew from a German translation. In that version, the cloth was invisible to anyone who was not the true son of his supposed father. Andersen changed the test so that the story focused on pride and the fear of looking foolish. Similar stories exist elsewhere too: an Indian version appears in a collection of fables written in 1283.
安徒生在 1837 年發表了這個故事，和〈小美人魚〉一起出版。他以一個 1335 年的中世紀西班牙故事為本，是從德文譯本讀到的。在那個版本裡，那塊布是「不是父親親生兒子」的人看不見的。安徒生改變了這個考驗，讓故事聚焦在驕傲和害怕顯得愚蠢上。類似的故事在別處也有：一個印度版本出現在一部寫於 1283 年的寓言集中。

Psychologists have a name for what happens in the crowd: pluralistic ignorance. Everyone privately doubts the clothes, but each person assumes that everyone else can see them. The phrase “the emperor has no clothes” is now used whenever a group pretends to believe something that no one really believes. The story reminds us that sometimes the most important voice is the one willing to state the obvious.
心理學家為群眾中發生的事取了一個名字：多數無知。每個人私下都懷疑那件衣服，卻都以為其他人看得到。如今，每當一群人假裝相信某件其實沒人相信的事時，人們就會說「國王沒穿衣服」。這個故事提醒我們：有時候最重要的聲音，是那個願意說出顯而易見事實的聲音。

advanced.title: Pluralistic Ignorance and the Courage of the Obvious
paras: Few fairy tales have entered everyday language as thoroughly as Hans Christian Andersen’s “The Emperor’s New Clothes”. First published in Copenhagen on 7 April 1837, in the same booklet as “The Little Mermaid”, it has since been translated into more than a hundred languages. Its central image — a ruler parading in invisible finery while his subjects applaud — has become shorthand for any situation in which a falsehood survives because no one is willing to name it. Andersen establishes his ruler’s priorities in a single joke: where people normally say a king is “sitting in council”, of this emperor they say he is “sitting in his wardrobe”.

很少有童話像安徒生的〈國王的新衣〉一樣，深深融入日常語言。它在 1837 年 4 月 7 日於哥本哈根首次出版，與〈小美人魚〉收在同一本小冊子裡，此後被翻譯成一百多種語言。它的核心意象——統治者穿著看不見的華服遊行，臣民則鼓掌叫好——已成為一種簡稱，用來形容任何因為沒人願意說破而得以存續的謊言。安徒生用一個笑話就交代了這位統治者的優先順序：一般人會說國王「正在議事」，而人們說這位皇帝「正坐在他的衣櫥裡」。

The mechanism of the swindle is psychologically precise. The supposed weavers claim their cloth is invisible to anyone “unfit for the office he held, or who was extraordinarily simple in character”. This turns perception into a test of competence. Each minister who inspects the empty looms faces the same dilemma: admitting the truth would expose him as incompetent, while pretending costs nothing. One by one, the officials, and finally the emperor himself, choose pretence, and each act of pretence makes the next more likely.
這場騙局的機制在心理上精準無比。假織工聲稱，他們的布凡是「不適任其職位，或天性特別單純」的人都看不見。這把「看見」變成了一場能力的測驗。每一位檢查空織布機的大臣，都面臨同樣的兩難：承認真相會暴露自己不適任，而假裝則毫無代價。官員們一個接一個——最後連國王本人——都選擇了假裝，而每一次假裝，都讓下一次假裝更有可能發生。

Andersen adapted the plot from a tale of 1335 in the Spanish Libro de los ejemplos by Juan Manuel, which he encountered in German translation. In the source, the cloth is invisible to any man who is not the son of his presumed father, so the fear at stake is of illegitimacy. Andersen’s alteration is revealing. By making the test one of fitness for office and intelligence, he shifted the satire towards courtly pride and intellectual vanity, vices that belong not to one king but to entire institutions.
安徒生的情節改編自胡安．曼努埃爾的西班牙《範例集》中一則 1335 年的故事，他是讀了德文譯本才知道的。在原始版本中，那塊布是「不是推定父親親生兒子」的男人看不見的，所以人們害怕的是被揭穿私生。安徒生的改動很有啟發性：把考驗改成是否適任與是否聰明，他把諷刺的矛頭轉向了宮廷的驕傲與知識上的虛榮——這些惡習不只屬於一位國王，而屬於整個體制。

Modern psychology offers a name for the crowd’s behaviour: pluralistic ignorance, a situation in which most members of a group privately reject a belief but wrongly assume that most others accept it. Everyone in the procession doubts the clothes; no one knows that everyone else doubts them too. The child’s cry — “But the Emperor has nothing at all on!” — works not because it reveals new information, but because it makes private knowledge public. Once spoken aloud, the truth spreads instantly through the crowd. The child’s father immediately recognises its significance: “Listen to the voice of innocence!”
現代心理學為群眾的行為取了一個名字：多數無知——群體中大多數成員私下拒絕某個信念，卻誤以為大多數其他人都接受它。遊行中的每個人都懷疑那件衣服；卻沒有人知道其他人也同樣懷疑。小孩的那聲叫喊——「可是國王什麼都沒穿啊！」——之所以有效，不是因為它揭露了新資訊，而是因為它把私下的認知變成公開的事實。一旦被大聲說出，真相就立刻在人群中傳開。孩子的父親立刻意識到這句話的意義：「聽聽這天真無邪的聲音！」

Andersen’s ending, however, resists a simple triumph. The emperor knows the people are right, yet he decides that the procession must go on, and his chamberlains hold up a train that is not there. Exposure does not automatically produce change; institutions can continue performing their rituals even after the illusion has collapsed. The tale therefore teaches two lessons at once: that stating the obvious can require real courage, and that truth, once spoken, still depends on people willing to act on it.
然而，安徒生的結局拒絕了簡單的勝利。國王知道人們說得對，卻決定遊行必須繼續，他的內侍們也繼續托著一條不存在的衣襬。被揭穿並不會自動帶來改變；即使幻象已經破滅，體制仍可能繼續演出它們的儀式。因此，這個故事同時教了兩件事：說出顯而易見的事實可能需要真正的勇氣；而真相一旦被說出，仍然有賴於願意依此行動的人。
